title: Compile-Time Guarantees with Type-State
goal: Understand how to encode object state into generic type parameters.

source.attribution: adapted from API Guidelines: Type Safety

sections.text: In object-oriented code, calling `send()` on an unauthenticated connection throws a runtime error. In Rust, you can make invalid states impossible to represent.

sections.caption: Zero-sized structs act as type markers for state.

sections.text: You implement methods only for specific states. Method calls transition the object from one generic state type to another by consuming `self`.

sections.caption: Consuming self moves ownership to the new type-state.

sections.text: Attempting to call methods on the wrong state causes compile error `E0599`. The compiler prevents state bugs before your program runs.

explanation: Understand how to encode object state into generic type parameters.
